response_text: To pass an argument into a thread, the user designs their thread function to accept a single void pointer parameter. This pointer can point to any data type or structure the user wants to pass. When creating the thread, the user provides a pointer to the data as the argument. On the operating system side, during thread creation, the OS allocates and sets up the thread’s stack. It specifically places the pointer to the argument in the location on the stack corresponding to the processor register R0, which is used to pass the first argument in the ARM calling convention. This ensures that when the thread starts executing, the argument pointer is already in the correct register for the thread function to access. This works because the OS follows the ARM ABI rules for function calls, so the thread function receives the pointer seamlessly without the OS needing to know the data’s type or structure.\n
